hook: My $89 cabinet kit actually cost $180, here's why

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of kit label showing '200 sq ft coverage'
scenes.voiceover: The label says 200 square feet — that's about 20 to 25 doors and drawers.

scenes.visual_prompt: Wide shot of a full kitchen with a double run of upper and lower cabinets
scenes.voiceover: A double run of upper and lower cabinets almost always needs two kits, not one.

scenes.visual_prompt: Open window with a fan running while deglosser fumes visibly waft, person wearing a mask
scenes.voiceover: Reviewers all say the same thing: the deglosser smell needs real airflow, not a cracked window.

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of bond coat being applied in thin, even strokes, slightly tacky texture visible
scenes.voiceover: The bond coat has to go on thin, two or three light coats, or it stays tacky.

scenes.visual_prompt: Calendar graphic flipping from Day 1 to Day 21 with cabinet doors off hinges throughout
scenes.voiceover: Dry to touch is 2 hours. Full cure is 1 to 3 weeks, with doors off the hinges that whole time.

scenes.visual_prompt: Trash bag being tied off with solvent rags and tape visible inside, placed outside
scenes.voiceover: And solvent-soaked rags don't sit in the kitchen trash can for a week — bag them as you go.

scenes.visual_prompt: Final cost graphic showing $89 plus $91 equals $180
scenes.voiceover: Budget $180 and three weeks, not $89 and a weekend.

caption: The $89 price tag on this cabinet kit is the headline, not the real number. Between the second kit most kitchens need and the actual cure time, I'm budgeting closer to $180 and three weeks before I'd call it finished. What reviewers wish they'd known before starting, on the blog.
